content:
Alex: Quick heads-up — I'll start the primary shift now (on until ~16:00 PT). there's an active degradation on hosted runtime (gen endpoints). error rate up ~6% over baseline. paging infra and support.

Priya: Saw it too, digging into router errors. can we confirm if this is a model-specific regression or infra?

Alex: Initial signals point at the runtime shard in us-west2. latency spikes and 5xxs mainly on /v1/generate. model seems fine locally.

infra-bot: [incident created] Incident 4321 — Increased 5xx on hosted runtime — severity: P2 — pages sent to oncall.

Jon: pinging infra oncall — @Lina are you able to pick this up as infra primary?

Lina: I'm on it. seeing elevated CPU on gpu-node-14 and kernel OOM events around 11:12. collecting dmesg + container logs now.

Sam: support-oncall here — triaging customer tickets. a handful report generation failures; most are retries so impact is partial. customers A and C opened severity-high tickets.

Priya: runtime vs infra routing question: if this is kernel/oom -> infra owns node remediation (drain/restart), runtime should own graceful fallback and persistent errors. who should handle rollback to a lower-memory model variant?

Lina: infra will coordinate node-level actions (drain, replace, kernel logs). runtime team should handle model routing and can flip fallback policies. @Alex you want to run the fallback?

Alex: I'll coordinate runtime fallback. Plan: 1) enable prefix KV caching to reduce load (short term) 2) route traffic from problematic shard to replica pool 3) if errors persist, switch to model-quantized-1.2 variant for heavy routes.

Jon: security note — if we're seeing OOMs that correlate with unusual request patterns, sec team wants request samples. @sec-oncall are you tracking anything suspicious?

sec-oncall: not yet. please collect and redact PII; send sample payloads to our secure channel. we'll look for exfiltration or malformed tokens.

Priya: runbook pointer for on-call handoff: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/oncall-handoff — remember to update the top-level status, set OWNERS, and explicitly note coverage gaps.

Alex: Current coverage: primary (me), secondary (Priya), infra (Lina), security (sec-oncall), support (support-oncall). gap: no mobile SDK lead on this shift — could affect SDK-related regressions.

Sam: I can loop in mobile-eng if needed. for now support will keep customers updated with templated message: "We're investigating increased 5xx for generation endpoints; engineer update in 15-30m."

Lina: infra actions so far: drained gpu-node-14, reprovisioning to gpu-node-22; kernel logs point to memory fragmentation, not suspicious. I've attached a snippet: 
```
[ 11.12.3456 ] Out of memory: Killed process 6712 (runtime-worker) total-vm: 42272kB, anon-rss: 38400kB
```

Alex: Runtime mitigations: enabling strict batching caps and prefix cache; initiating route shift for 10% -> replica pool now.

ops-bot: Route-shift job queued (job-id: rs-20260314-01).

Priya: Cross-team routing question we should capture in the post-incident: who owns the automated rollback trigger thresholds? runtime or infra? my vote: threshold *detection* infra (node health), *rollback execution* runtime (model variants).

Jon: agree. add to action items. Also schedule a short postmortem with runtime/infra/support/security to flesh out ownership boundaries.

sec-oncall: found a few malformed auth headers in samples, likely client retries causing spikes. not malicious but helpful to know for mitigation.

Alex: Action items captured in incident doc: https://redwood.internal/incidents/4321 (add your notes). Handoff to Priya in 20m — Priya, you okay to be primary until 20:00 PT if this persists?

Priya: I can extend, but I need someone to be secondary for infra followups after my shift. Lina can you stay for 30m?

Lina: I can, but after that I'll need relief. tagging @Jon for infra backup after 16:30.

Jon: can do. I'll be on-call-ready at 16:25.

Sam: I'll keep customer comms and update tickets every 30m.

Alex: Great. quick checklist for handoff in 20m: - update OWNERS in incident doc - note current mitigations + tentative rollback plan - list coverage gap (mobile lead) - leave link to runbook + log snippets.

Priya: One more cross-team question: for future incidents, can we add a routing matrix to the runbook that maps symptom -> owning team? (e.g., OOM/kernel -> infra, model quality/regression -> runtime, auth/token anomalies -> security/support).

Jon: +1. I'll draft a PR to the runbook after this is stable.

Alex: thanks all — I'll drop final handoff note here in 18m. :thumbsup:
